requirements.requirement: New user passwords on node1 must be at least 12 characters long.
requirements.summary: The active pwquality configuration sets minlen=12, pam_pwquality is enabled in the PAM password stack, and an 11-character four-class password was rejected for being shorter than 12 both before and after reboot.

requirements.requirement: New user passwords on node1 must contain at least three character classes.
requirements.summary: The active configuration sets minclass=3, and a 14-character two-class password was rejected specifically for having fewer than three classes. A compliant four-class control was accepted before and after reboot.

overall_summary: Both password-policy outcomes are satisfied. The policy is integrated into PAM, directly validated at the relevant failure boundaries, and remained effective after node1 rebooted. Restart evidence shows a healthy pre-restart state, scheduled restart, observed downtime, a changed boot identity, and recovered system, SSH, PAM, and policy state; the fixed lifecycle boot observations independently agree.
limitations: Functional rejection and acceptance were tested with pwscore against the system policy rather than through a complete interactive user password-change transaction. The active PAM rule provides strong supporting evidence that the tested policy governs new-password changes.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Installing libpam-pwquality and its dependencies was necessary to enforce the policy; editing pwquality.conf established the required settings; installing libpwquality-tools supported bounded functional verification; and rebooting fulfilled the mandatory restart protocol. The failed initial pwscore attempt only created temporary output files that the same command removed. Final lifecycle observations show no failed services, package damage, unsafe new listeners, or abandoned temporary files.
